questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English speaking country, preferably overseas, and I choose Canada because of its beautiful nature and kind population

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got everything out of the exchange that I wanted: I met some great people, explored Canada and its beautiful nature, and got the "campus-experience" at the university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy - the international student advisors were very helpful, and I got a ton of emails with all the relevant information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university hosted some great orientation events, both for international students and for "normal" students, which was really helpful and a great way to get familiar with campus while at the same time meeting new friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing market in Victoria is pretty crazy! because a lot of students were returning to the city after being in lockdown for the previous year, both new and old students needed to find housing, and there was a real state of panic for many people.Especially because there also is a shortage of on-campus housing, and the uni didn't offer any help. However, I didn't actually find it too difficult, possibly because people took pity on me being an internationl student. The

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend finding housing close to campus. It is just nice to be close to everything happening, and not stressing too much about pulic transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about housing, it'll work out in the end!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As an undergraduate student you have to fill out some papers that prove you meet the prerequisites for the courses you want to take. A bit of a bother. As a graduate student, I found it a bit difficult to figure out, if they would approve me for the courses I wanted to take, but generally I got the sense that if it is in your area of expertice, they are very happe to let you register for graduate courses as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international advisors were very helpful with this proces. And extremely fast at answering emails, which was really nice!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I found it to be a bit of a long proces, so be prepared for that and allocate the necessary time for it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took masters courses, and I found the level to be equivalent, if not a bit more advanced, than KU. Especially the students were all very well prepared, engaged in the courses and at a high academic level. Most graduate students at uvic do research, which I found to be a bit daunting - but so much to learn from them!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the graduate courses were very different. Small classes, usually no more than 5-10 people, and you actually get to have a relation with the professor, which I found very awarding. However the small class size and discussion-based type of courses also means that there is expected much more of you, you have to read and come prepared for class, and actively engage in discussion. Different that KU, but I think I learned more this way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking! The area arouond victoria has so many good hiking options. Visit Vancouver, squamish and whistler. Banff is a longer trip, but definitely worth it! best thing i did.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I wasn't prepared for the big roads, lots of trafic and the many cars. the city is nice, but doesn't have that "European charm", which i missed a bit

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the orientation events and join clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: no particular thing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are so friendly! So very lovely and heartwarming

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: on't make studying you number 1 priority - there is so much else to experience while being on exchange! See the country, make friends, enjoy the nature!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: you're gonna spend much more money than you expect - but it's worth it!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting a group of friends with which i felt connected with and explored with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my boyfriend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it, it's amazing!
